sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-FLAG surface staining on intact cells confirmed surface display; NTF membrane retention after Px-mediated proteolysis was unaffected. No CDCP1 signaling/kinase function assay was reported for the FLAG-tagged construct specifically.
sites.rationale: CDCP1 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with a signal peptide spanning residues 1–29; the mature N-terminus begins at F30. An 'N-terminal FLAG tag' on a surface-displayed, membrane-anchored construct must be inserted after signal peptide cleavage (insert_after_residue = 29), placing the tag at the extracellular mature N-terminus. Python verification confirms seq[28]='A' (position 29, last SP residue) and seq[29]='F' (position 30, first mature extracellular residue). The site is 638 residues from the TM boundary (668), well within the extracellular domain. L3 directly confirms surface accessibility by anti-FLAG staining on intact cells. Full-length CDCP1 with an N-terminal FLAG tag (and R368/K369 replaced by a PreScission Protease site) was stably expressed in HEK293T and other human cell lines. Anti-FLAG staining of intact cells confirmed that the FLAG-tagged N-terminal fragment (NTF) remains membrane-associated and surface-accessible after proteolysis.

sources.claim: Despite this, staining by anti5 FLAG and IgG 4A06 were unaffected with Px treatment, indicating that the NTF remains membrane-associated after proteolysis.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 describe the same N-terminal FLAG-tagged CDCP1 construct as L3 (preprint vs. published paper); L3 was chosen as the single supporting clip because it is the most probative, directly confirming surface display. L4 (FLAG-tagged CDCP1-Y734F) does not state the FLAG tag position and cannot be used to pin a junction; Y734 is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. L5 (CDCP1res-F and CDCP1res-HA) does not state tag positions and yields no pinnable site. L6 (ΔECD-FLAG) is a deletion construct lacking the extracellular domain; the tag position is unstated and the construct is not full-length, so no surface site can be derived from it.

literature_other_positions.note: Y734 is a Src-family kinase phosphorylation site in the intracellular domain (residues 689–836); L4 describes a FLAG-tagged CDCP1-Y734F mutant expressed in HeLa cells, but the FLAG tag position is unstated and Y734 itself is cytoplasmic, not a surface tag site.
